case_analysis.focal_point: Whether the mandatory consecutive sentencing provision in 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1)(D)(ii) applies when a defendant is convicted and sentenced under 18 U.S.C. § 924(j) for causing death through the use of a firearm during a drug trafficking crime.
case_analysis.petitioner_position: Efrain Lora argues that the consecutive sentencing mandate of 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1)(D)(ii) does not apply to sentences imposed under 18 U.S.C. § 924(j). He contends that § 924(j) is a distinct offense that does not automatically trigger the consecutive sentencing requirement of § 924(c), thereby allowing for judicial discretion in sentencing or the possibility of concurrent sentences. Petitioner also invokes the rule of lenity, suggesting any ambiguity in the statute should be resolved in favor of the defendant.
case_analysis.respondent_position: The United States argues that the consecutive sentencing provision in 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1)(D)(ii) does apply to sentences under 18 U.S.C. § 924(j). The government asserts that the Second Circuit's decision, which mandated a consecutive sentence, is consistent with the interpretation adopted by the majority of other circuits. They also contend that the rule of lenity is inapplicable because there is no 'grievous ambiguity or uncertainty' in the statute's text, structure, history, or purpose.
